subject: Operationalization recap & SLO/topology confirmation - LumenTech
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom@lumentech.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, eng-team@lumentech.com
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the call — follow-up on SLOs, model footprint, and topology

Sean / Irene —

Thanks for the deep-dive today. Quick notes from our side while its fresh:

Pain points we confirmed on the call:
- Tail latency spikes during peak events (our 95th/99th jump 3-5x) when sequence lengths are higher than expected.
- Cost unpredictability as we scale from staging to prod — our infra budget is capped and we need tighter token/unit forecasts.
- Model drift: guardrails around model rollouts/testing before customer exposure.

Goals (what success looks like for LumenTech):
- Stable P95 < 200ms for single-turn queries at 512 tokens, with autoscale headroom for 2x baseline QPS.
- Ability to route lower-priority inference to quantized variants with fallback to full precision if quality drops.
- Clear observability: per-route token breakdown + per-model error/latency traces.

As next steps, can you share an ops-level sketch for:
1) Expected topology for a canary->prod rollout (including fallback behavior).
2) A short cost estimate for the steady-state (QPS 80) vs burst (QPS 240) scenario.
3) Any pre-flight telemetry we should collect on our side (prom/trace spans, typical sequence length histograms).

I attached a short MOP (current) and a spreadsheet with our 3-month traffic profile.

Tom
Director of Engineering
LumenTech Solutions

Attachment: lumentech-mop-v1.pdf (PDF, 320KB)
Attachment: kv-cache-estimates.xlsx (XLSX, 72KB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — follow-up on SLOs, model footprint, and topology

Tom —

Appreciate the crisp summary. Short recap from our side and concrete next steps so everyone has alignment:

Confirmed pain / success metrics (agreed):
- Target: P95 <= 200ms at 512 tokens; P99 target depends on async fallback but aim for <= 450ms.
- Baseline steady QPS: 80 (prod), burst 240 (short windows).
- Acceptable quality delta for quantized variants: up to 2% drop in pass-rate on the judge prompt set.

Topology sketch (high level):
1) Ingress: edge LB -> route by SLA tag (latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive).
2) Fast-path: pinned model variant on Dedicated pool with warm KV cache (preferred for latency-sensitive routes).
3) Cost-path: quantized variant (lower VRAM) on mixed GPU pool; auto-fallback to fast-path on error/quality degrades.
4) Canary: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated regression checks (latency, top-token divergence).

Telemetry to collect (from LumenTech):
- Real request traces with seq_len, tokens_out, model_variant, and model_latency_ms.
- Distribution histograms for input seq length and customer-specific QPS windows.
- A small eval set (50-100 prompts) for pre/post quantization quality checks.

Deliverables well provide by EOD Fri:
- Ops sketch PDF with fallback rules and redis/KV sizing estimates.
- Two cost scenarios (steady & burst) with bucketized cost per million tokens and expected GPU-hours.
- Short checklist of traces/metrics to instrument.

Ccd Irene and Grace to coordinate on the quantization/ops sizing work. If that works, well loop in Solutions to draft a mutual action plan.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tom / Sean —

Adding a few technical details and a short checklist wed like LumenTech to produce so we can run accurate capacity/cost modeling:

Checklist for LumenTech (small data items):
- 72-hour sampled trace (fields: request_id, seq_len_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, model_name). If sampling is hard, even aggregated histograms by 5-minute buckets will work.
- Typical payload sizes for embeddings vs generative calls (if you use both).
- Any compliance constraints: data residency or retention windows that would affect Private deployment.

Quantization note: we recommend testing 4-bit quantization for cost-path first. For your judge set, well run A/B on the canary to measure the pass-rate impact.

Ill attach the ops-sketch and a small template for the sample trace.

Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Tom —

Thanks again for the time. Quick operational notes / asks before we produce the cost scenarios:
- Please confirm whether your burst windows are predictable (scheduled marketing pushes) or ad-hoc; if scheduled, include the calendar/cron pattern.
- Can you share a 7-day QPS heatmap from your staging environment (UTC). Thats the most helpful signal for batching and autoscale policy recommendations.
- If you have any existing model evaluation suites, please attach (even a README is helpful).

Immediate deliverable timeline from Redwood:
- Ops sketch + fallback rules: by EOD Fri Apr 21 (Irene + Sean).
- Cost scenarios + expected GPU-hours: by Mon Apr 24 (Grace).
- Draft mutual action plan to land POC: will send Wed Apr 26.

If those dates look OK, Ill schedule a 30-minute sync next week to walk through the ops sketch.

Best,
Grace Oconnor
